issues_detected.description: No numeric file size (bytes) provided. Instance/count metadata is only embedded in narrative descriptions (e.g. '17 genes', '72/100 chromatin modifiers', 'over 1,000 protein complexes', '11,739 targeted genes') rather than as a structured file-size or instance-count field.
issues_detected.recommendation: Add explicit bytes or instance-count fields per distribution to enable programmatic size estimation.

issues_detected.description: distribution_formats describe multiple data modalities and platforms (RO-Crate/JSON-LD, MassIVE MS data, NCBI SRA sequence data, NDEx network/CX maps, Dataverse), but the explicit distribution-level format/media_type fields are homogeneous (all ZIP / application/zip), understating the true file-type variety.
issues_detected.recommendation: Record per-platform media types (application/ld+json for RO-Crate metadata, mzML/mzid for MS, FASTQ for SRA, CX/CX2 for NDEx) rather than labelling every distribution ZIP.

issues_detected.description: Ethics coverage is strong for de-identified commercial cell lines but there is no dedicated ethical_reviews/IRB field and no informed_consent chain for the original donors. This is largely appropriate given human_subject_research=No and de-identified commercial sourcing, but the donor-provenance consent chain is undocumented.
issues_detected.recommendation: Note the original donor consent basis for the source cell lines (ATCC / HipSci) or state explicitly that formal IRB/consent is not applicable and why.

issues_detected.description: RRID identifiers use the CVCL_ (Cellosaurus) namespace (RRID:CVCL_0419, RRID:CVCL_B5P3) rather than the SCR_/AB_ patterns cited in the rubric. CVCL_ is the correct and expected RRID namespace for cell lines, so this is valid, not an error.
issues_detected.recommendation: No change needed; CVCL RRIDs are appropriate for cell-line identification.

Cell-line RRIDs (CVCL_0419 for MDA-MB-468, CVCL_B5P3 for KOLF2.1J) are valid Cellosaurus identifiers and semantically appropriate for provenance.
Provenance is robustly documented via FAIRSCAPE RO-Crates, ARK persistent identifiers, and the EVI Evidence Graph Ontology with end-to-end provenance entailments.

strengths: Exceptional structural completeness: all mandatory fields populated with substantive content and 26 diverse keywords.
Comprehensive funding and attribution: specific NIH grant numbers, award amounts, and 24 creators with ORCIDs and affiliations.
Outstanding technical documentation: detailed collection protocols, named labs, versioned instruments, and preprocessing tools including a specific IMP version (2.18).
Strong FAIR compliance: versioned persistent DOIs, RO-Crate/FAIRSCAPE provenance with EVI evidence graphs, and cross-platform interlinking (Dataverse, NDEx, MassIVE, SRA).
Internally consistent ethics/governance logic appropriate to de-identified commercial cell-line data (no HIPAA/FDA obligations, de-identification confirmed, named governance contact).
Multiple DOI-linked publications including a peer-reviewed Nature article and an explicit dataset citation requirement.
weaknesses: No numeric file-size (bytes) metadata; instance counts appear only within narrative descriptions.
Distribution-level format/media_type fields are homogeneous (all ZIP), understating the multimodal file-type variety.
No dedicated ethical_reviews/IRB field or documented donor informed-consent chain (largely appropriate for the data type, but a provenance gap).
recommendations: Add per-distribution bytes or instance-count fields to enable programmatic size estimation.
Record platform-specific media types (application/ld+json, mzML/mzid, FASTQ, CX/CX2) rather than labelling every distribution ZIP.
State the donor consent basis for the source cell lines (ATCC/HipSci) or explicitly document why formal IRB/consent is not applicable.
Add a confidentiality_level classification to complete the access-governance metadata.
